preamble: The grid is to be seen as consisting of four 6 x 6 quadrants. Clues are of four different types, determined by the quadrant within which their initial letters fall, with one exception (see below). Solvers must discover which clue belongs to which quadrant/type. Clue types are as follows: A. Normal cryptic. B. Misprints: each clue contains a misprint of one letter, always occurring in the definition part; answers are to be entered correctly spelt. C. Anagrams: in each clue the definition part leads to the answer to be entered and the (cryptic) remainder leads to a one-word anagram of this answer. D. Printer’s Devilry: each clue is a passage from which the printer has removed a hidden answer, closing the gap and sometimes taking liberties with the punctuation, but not disturbing the order of the remaining letters. Example: Vaulting above tunnel entrance appears inane, scary. Answer: PESTO. Undevilled version: Vaulting above tunnel entrance appears in an escape story. Every passage, when complete, makes sense. One answer has the wrong type of clue for the quadrant in which it begins. Competitors should submit with their solutions a clue to this word of the correct type for its position in the diagram.
